intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace and rent a traditional Hanbok to wear while strolling through the palace grounds. Wearing Hanbok grants free entry, making it a budget-friendly deep dive into Korean royal culture and history.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through one of Seoul's oldest and most vibrant traditional markets, sampling iconic Korean street foods such as bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). A true immersion into local food culture.

experiences.name: K-Pop Dance Class & Idol District Exploration
experiences.description: Take a beginner K-Pop dance class at one of the many studios in the Hongdae area, then explore the neighborhood's street performances, indie music venues, K-pop merchandise shops, and vibrant youth culture scene — the heartbeat of Korean pop culture.

experiences.name: Bukchon Hanok Village Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the beautifully preserved traditional Korean village of Bukchon, featuring hundreds of historic hanok (traditional wooden houses). Visit small cultural workshops offering hands-on experiences in Korean tea ceremony, pottery, or hanji (traditional paper) crafts.

experiences.name: Han River Picnic & Sunset Cruise
experiences.description: Join locals for a classic Han River picnic with convenience store snacks and instant noodles — a beloved Korean pastime. Follow it with an evening cruise along the Han River to enjoy panoramic city views, glittering bridges, and a stunning Seoul sunset from the water.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00 at Incheon International Airport
day_by_day.afternoon: Take AREX (Airport Railroad Express) from Incheon to Gyeongbokgung area (~60 min, ~₩9,500). Check in to Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Freshen up and take a short orientation walk around the Gyeongbokgung Palace exterior walls and Gwanghwamun Square to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Insadong alley (10 min walk from hotel) — a charming cultural street full of traditional crafts, tea houses, and street snacks. Pick up a Hotteok (sweet pancake, ~₩1,500) from a street vendor for a quick snack.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport — try a convenience store (GS25 or CU) kimbap set (~₩3,000–₩4,000)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market (15 min walk) — try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and mayak gimbap at the market stalls (~₩8,000–₩12,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-money card at the airport (₩4,000 deposit) and load ₩30,000 for easy subway and bus travel. December in Seoul is cold (0°C to -5°C), so pack thermals and a heavy coat. The AREX direct train is fastest; avoid taxis which can cost ₩70,000+.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (opens 9:00, admission ₩3,000). Witness the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 and 14:00 (free with palace entry). Explore the grand palace grounds including Geunjeongjeon throne hall and the beautiful Hyangwonjeong pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace grounds (free with palace ticket). Then head to Bukchon Hanok Village (free, 10 min walk) — a stunning neighborhood of traditional Korean houses. Rent a hanbok for photos (~₩15,000/hr from nearby shops).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Samcheongdong-gil street for indie cafes and small galleries. End the evening at a cozy pojangmacha (street food tent) near Anguk Station for tteokbokki and odeng (fish cake soup).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store triangle kimbap + instant coffee (~₩3,000)
meals.lunch: Packed dosirak (lunch box) from a nearby kimbap restaurant near the palace (~₩5,000–₩7,000)
meals.dinner: Pojangmacha near Anguk Station — tteokbokki, odeng, and soondae combo (~₩8,000–₩10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is free on the last Wednesday of each month. Wear comfortable shoes — the palace grounds are large. The hanbok rental shops near Gyeongbokgung offer free palace entry when wearing one.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon) — guided tours available in English (~₩8,000 combined ticket). The winter landscape of the Secret Garden is hauntingly beautiful. Book the garden tour slot in advance online.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Changgyeonggung Palace next door (₩1,000 entry) — a quieter, less-touristy palace. Then head to Jongmyo Shrine (₩1,000), a UNESCO World Heritage site where Joseon kings are enshrined — deeply atmospheric and culturally significant.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) area via subway (Dongdaemun History & Culture Park station). The futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed building is free to walk around. Browse the nearby Dongdaemun night markets for budget shopping and street food.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store egg sandwich and banana milk (~₩3,500)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village nearby — try a small Korean set meal (백반, baekban) at a local restaurant (~₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun night market street food — try dak-kkochi (grilled chicken skewers), tteokbokki, and fried foods (~₩8,000–₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Garden tour has limited spots — book via the official Changdeokgung website. Jongmyo Shrine has free guided tours on Saturdays. DDP is spectacular lit up at night in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (Line 2, ~25 min from Anguk). Explore the vibrant youth culture district — street art, indie music culture, and quirky cafes. Visit the free outdoor performance area and Hongik University's art street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area — the campus is architecturally stunning and free to enter. Browse the ECC (Ewha Campus Complex) underground building. Then explore the trendy Yeonnam-dong neighborhood (10 min walk) known for its cafe alley and indie vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for Friday night street performances (buskers perform nightly near the main park, especially on weekends). The atmosphere is electric with K-indie music acts.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae area cafe — try an Egg Drop sandwich (~₩5,500) or similar brunch cafe
meals.lunch: Sinchon area — try a jjajangmyeon (black bean noodles) and tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) combo at a Chinese-Korean restaurant (~₩9,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae pojangmacha alley — samgyeopsal (pork belly) at a budget BBQ spot with soju (~₩12,000–₩15,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae on a Friday night is a peak K-culture experience — street performances, buskers, and youth energy. Yeonnam-dong is Instagram-famous but genuinely charming. Keep your T-money card loaded.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market (Hoehyeon Station, Line 4) — one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets. Great for cheap shopping: dried seafood, clothing, accessories, and street food. Open from early morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Myeongdong (5 min from Namdaemun) — Korea's most famous shopping district. While shops can be pricey, the outdoor street food stalls are excellent and budget-friendly. Try cheese lobster, tornado potato, and Korean corn dogs.
day_by_day.evening: Visit N Seoul Tower on Namsan Mountain. Take the Namsan Cable Car (₩9,500 round trip) or hike up for free (~30 min). The tower observation deck costs ₩16,000 but the outdoor plaza and city views are free and magical at night. Attach a love lock if you wish.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market — haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) and kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) from market stalls (~₩6,000–₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food crawl — budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 for multiple snacks: Korean corn dog, tteokbokki, gyeran-ppang (egg bread)
meals.dinner: Near Myeongdong — try a budget Korean BBQ restaurant or a hearty sundubu-jjigae (soft tofu stew) set meal (~₩9,000–₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Namdaemun Market is best experienced early morning. Myeongdong street food vendors are most active in the afternoon and evening. The free hike up Namsan is beautiful but icy in December — wear grippy shoes or bring micro-spikes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park (Gupabal Station, Line 3). Take a winter hike on the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail — stunning mountain fortress walls with panoramic Seoul views. Entry is free. The hike to Daedongmun Gate takes about 2–3 hours round trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Seoul. Visit Seochon Village (서촌) — a quieter, more authentic alternative to Bukchon, with traditional hanok homes, indie bookshops, and local cafes. Visit Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House, former presidential residence) — now open to the public for free.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in the Gyeongbokgung/Insadong area near your hotel. Visit a Korean jjimjilbang (sauna/bathhouse) like Siloam Sauna near Seoul Station (~₩12,000) for a truly local experience — soak in hot baths and rest in the heated common room.

meals.breakfast: Pack convenience store kimbap and a hot canned coffee for the hike (~₩4,000)
meals.lunch: Trail snacks + ramen from a mountain hut near the fortress (many hikers stop here, ~₩4,000–₩6,000)
meals.dinner: Seochon Village — try a local doenjang-jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) set meal at a neighborhood restaurant (~₩8,000–₩10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan in December can have snow and ice — hiking poles are recommended. Start the hike before 10:00 to avoid crowds. The Blue House (Cheong Wa Dae) requires advance online reservation for guided tours.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a hip neighborhood of renovated hanok houses turned into cafes, cocktail bars, and boutiques. Morning is the quietest time to explore. Visit a traditional tea house for a cup of sikhye (sweet rice drink) or yuja-cha (yuzu tea).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dongdaemun (Line 1/4) to visit the Dongdaemun History & Culture Park and the free outdoor exhibits. Then visit Heunginjimun Gate (Dongdaemun Gate) — one of the original city gates of Seoul. Walk along the Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) back toward the city center — a peaceful elevated stream walkway.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Gwangjang Market for dinner — this is Seoul's most famous traditional market for food lovers. Try yukhoe (raw beef), bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), and mayak gimbap. The market is atmospheric and lively in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Ikseon-dong cafe — try traditional bingsu or a Korean-style breakfast set (~₩6,000–₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Cheonggyecheon Stream area — grab a quick bibimbap at a local restaurant (~₩8,000)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok + mayak gimbap + makgeolli (rice wine) (~₩12,000–₩15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Cheonggyecheon Stream is beautifully lit in winter evenings. Gwangjang Market is one of the most authentic food market experiences in Korea — go hungry. Makgeolli pairs perfectly with bindaetteok.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Itaewon (Line 6) — Seoul's most international neighborhood. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (₩10,000) for world-class Korean and contemporary art. Alternatively, explore the free street art and murals in the Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to Noksapyeong area and explore the Gyeongnidan-gil street — a trendy strip of international restaurants, vintage shops, and indie cafes. Browse the antique shops and flea markets in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hangang Park (Han River) — take Line 9 to Yeouinaru Station. Bundle up and enjoy the winter night view of the Han River. Rent a convenience store ramen cup, heat it up at the park kiosk, and enjoy it riverside like locals do. The lit-up Mapo Bridge and city skyline are beautiful.

meals.breakfast: Itaewon area bakery or cafe — try a croissant and Americano (~₩5,000–₩7,000)
meals.lunch: Gyeongnidan-gil — try a budget international option: Turkish doner kebab or Japanese ramen (~₩9,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Hangang Park convenience store experience — cup ramen, kimbap, and a warm canned drink (~₩6,000–₩8,000) — a quintessentially Korean experience

day_by_day.notes: Itaewon is Seoul's most multicultural neighborhood — great for experiencing a different side of the city. Hangang Park in winter is cold but magical — dress very warmly. The convenience store Han River experience is a beloved local tradition.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (Ichon Station, Line 4) — one of Asia's largest museums with 12,000+ artifacts. Admission is FREE. Spend 2–3 hours exploring Korean history from prehistoric times through the Joseon dynasty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Yongsan Family Park adjacent to the museum (free). Then head to the War Memorial of Korea (Samgakji Station, Line 4/6) — a powerful and extensive museum chronicling Korean military history. The outdoor exhibits with tanks, jets, and warships are free; indoor galleries are also free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Mangwon Market (near Hongdae) for a local evening market experience — less touristy than Gwangjang. Browse the food stalls and pick up fresh Korean street food. Then explore the nearby Mangwon-dong neighborhood for a local residential Seoul vibe.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or convenience store — yogurt, banana, and triangle kimbap (~₩3,000–₩4,000)
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals (~₩7,000–₩9,000) with a view of the museum garden
meals.dinner: Mangwon Market — try gimbap, pajeon, and tteokbokki from market stalls (~₩8,000–₩10,000)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is genuinely world-class and completely free — a budget traveler's dream. The War Memorial is emotionally impactful and important for understanding modern Korean history. Book ahead for popular restaurants in Mangwon-dong.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (도보 10분 from hotel) — the headquarters of Korean Buddhism and one of Seoul's most important temples. Free to enter. Watch monks perform morning rituals. The temple is beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Insadong main street more thoroughly — browse traditional craft shops, calligraphy stores, and the Ssamziegil courtyard (free to enter, indie shops inside). Pick up affordable souvenirs: tea sets, hanji paper crafts, and Korean snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a Korean Christmas Eve — Koreans celebrate it as a romantic holiday. Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream or Myeongdong for the festive Christmas lights and decorations. Myeongdong Cathedral is beautifully lit and open for visitors. Join the festive street atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Insadong tea house — traditional breakfast with rice porridge (juk) and side dishes (~₩8,000–₩10,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong Ssamziegil food court — try hoddeok (sweet pancake) and various Korean snacks (~₩6,000–₩8,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve splurge — try a Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) restaurant near Myeongdong (~₩15,000–₩20,000) — a popular Korean Christmas tradition

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve (크리스마스 이브) is one of the most festive nights in Seoul. Myeongdong and Cheonggyecheon are packed with couples and families. Korean Christmas tradition involves chimaek (chicken + beer) rather than turkey. Book any restaurant in advance tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — take the subway to Suwon Station (~45 min from Seoul, ~₩1,850). The UNESCO-listed fortress walls encircle the city and are free to walk. Climb the ramparts for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (행궁, ₩1,500) — a beautifully restored royal villa. Visit the Suwon Traditional Culture Center nearby for free cultural demonstrations. Walk through the traditional market inside the fortress walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Rest and refresh at the hotel. Head out for a quiet evening walk around Gyeongbokgung Palace walls lit up at night — a peaceful and beautiful winter scene.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — keep it light before the trip (~₩3,000–₩4,000)
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is famous for its beef short ribs. Try a budget portion at a local restaurant near the market (~₩12,000–₩15,000)
meals.dinner: Back in Seoul — quiet neighborhood restaurant near the hotel for a simple sundubu-jjigae (soft tofu stew) set (~₩8,000–₩10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is one of Korea's best-preserved fortresses and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The walk along the fortress walls takes 2–3 hours. Christmas Day in Korea is a public holiday — some smaller shops may be closed but markets and convenience stores are open.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World (잠실, Jamsil Station, Line 2/8) — Asia's largest indoor theme park. Day pass is ~₩62,000 (budget splurge day). Alternatively, the outdoor Magic Island area offers great views and is more affordable. The adjacent Lotte World Tower observation deck (Seoul Sky) is ₩27,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jamsil and the COEX Mall area (free to enter) — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. Visit the COEX Starfield Library — a stunning public library with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, completely free to visit and very Instagram-worthy.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam (강남) for the evening — walk the famous Gangnam-daero boulevard. Visit the Garosu-gil (가로수길) tree-lined street for trendy cafes and boutiques. Experience the polished, upscale side of Seoul that contrasts with the traditional areas you've explored.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — fuel up before a big day (~₩3,000–₩5,000)
meals.lunch: Lotte World food court or COEX food hall — Korean fast food options like bibimbap or noodles (~₩8,000–₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil, Gangnam — try a trendy but affordable Korean fusion restaurant or a classic samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) restaurant (~₩12,000–₩15,000)

day_by_day.notes: If skipping Lotte World to save budget, the COEX Starfield Library and Aquarium area are free/low-cost and worth the trip to Gangnam. Garosu-gil is one of Seoul's most photogenic streets, especially with winter decorations.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite neighborhood near the hotel. Take a slow walk through Gyeongbokgung area one last time. Visit the National Palace Museum of Korea (inside palace grounds, free) if you haven't already. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at Insadong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport. Take AREX from Seoul Station or Hongik University Station to Incheon (~60 min, ₩9,500 direct train). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Use remaining T-money balance on snacks at the airport convenience stores.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — try a local 해장국 (haejangguk, hangover soup) restaurant near the hotel for a hearty send-off (~₩8,000–₩10,000)
meals.lunch: Airport — try a proper Korean meal at one of the airport restaurants (prices are reasonable at ICN) — try Bibigo or a local brand (~₩10,000–₩13,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: The AREX direct train to the airport is the most reliable and budget-friendly option. You can do airport check-in at Seoul Station the day before via the City Airport Terminal service (saves time). Refund unused T-money balance at any subway station before departing. 안녕히 가세요! (Goodbye/Travel safely!)

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight LH lands at 13:00 at Incheon International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Incheon Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and exchange currency at the airport bank. Take the AREX (Airport Railroad Express) direct train to Gwanghwamun Station (~60 min, ~9,000 KRW). Check in to the Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu and freshen up. Take a gentle evening stroll around Gyeongbokgung Palace's outer walls and Gwanghwamun Square to get oriented. Admire the illuminated Gwanghwamun Gate and the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby Tongin Market alley for a relaxed first taste of Seoul street food. Walk through the charming Bukchon Hanok Village entrance streets, beautifully lit in the winter evening.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Incheon Airport food court – try a bowl of Bibimbap or Doenjang Jjigae (~8,000–12,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung – famous ginseng chicken soup, perfect for warming up after travel (~16,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag may be significant. Stay hydrated and avoid over-scheduling. The T-money card (rechargeable transit card) can be purchased at the airport convenience store for seamless subway and bus travel throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) right at your doorstep – arrive for the 10:00 Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at Gwanghwamun Gate. Explore the grand palace grounds including Geunjeongjeon Throne Hall, Gyeonghoeru Pavilion (stunning in winter), and the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace grounds (free with palace ticket ~3,000 KRW). Consider renting a Hanbok at one of the nearby rental shops for free palace entry and great photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the National Palace Museum of Korea (free admission) adjacent to Gyeongbokgung. Then walk north to explore Bukchon Hanok Village – wander the traditional alleyways lined with centuries-old Korean houses. Stop at a small café for hot Sikhye (sweet rice drink) or Yujacha (citron tea).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down Insadong (인사동) – Seoul's cultural street filled with art galleries, traditional craft shops, and teahouses. Visit Ssamziegil, an artsy courtyard mall with indie shops. Browse for Korean souvenirs, calligraphy art, and handmade goods.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel – try a Korean-style breakfast with toast, eggs, and coffee at a local bakery like Paris Baguette or Isaac Toast (~5,000–8,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Gyeongbokgung Palace area – Jilsiru Tteok Café for traditional rice cake set lunch (~12,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Insadong area – Sanchon (산촌) Buddhist temple cuisine restaurant for a unique multi-course vegetarian Korean meal (~25,000–35,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays, but it's Wednesday today – great timing. Dress warmly as December temperatures in Seoul can drop to -5°C to 5°C. Hanbok rental shops open around 9:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) – book the Secret Garden tour in advance online (~8,000 KRW). The winter garden with bare trees and frozen ponds has a serene, ethereal beauty. Explore Injeongjeon Hall and the palace's intimate courtyards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the adjacent Changgyeonggung Palace (창경궁, ~1,000 KRW) and then cross over to Jongmyo Shrine (종묘) – the UNESCO-listed royal ancestral shrine, one of the most sacred and atmospheric sites in Seoul. Enjoy the solemn, minimalist architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) – Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark. Explore the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun Market area, which comes alive at night with fashion stalls and street vendors. Walk around the lit-up DDP for dramatic night photos.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area – Noryangjin or local pojangmacha (street food stall) style breakfast with Hotteok (sweet pancake) and soybean milk (~3,000–5,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Near Jongmyo Shrine – Gwangjang Market (광장시장), one of Seoul's oldest traditional markets. Try Mayak Gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), Bindaetteok (mung bean pancake), and Japchae (~5,000–10,000 KRW per dish)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area – Pyoungjin Halmae Nakji (평진할매낙지) for spicy stir-fried octopus (Nakji Bokkeum) with rice (~12,000–15,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour online at least a few days in advance as slots fill up quickly. Gwangjang Market is a must-visit food experience – go hungry!

day_by_day.morning: Explore Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) – take the subway to Gupabal Station and hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail. The winter mountain scenery with snow-dusted peaks and ancient stone fortress walls is spectacular. A moderate 3–4 hour hike to Daedongmun Gate and back is rewarding without being too strenuous.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the Seochon Village (서촌) – a charming, less-touristy neighborhood west of Gyeongbokgung. Browse independent bookshops, art studios, and traditional tea houses. Visit Suseongdong Valley, a small hidden stream valley within the village.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Seochon's café district. Visit Tongui-dong Butter Lane (통의동 버터레인) for artisan coffee and desserts. Walk back to the hotel through the illuminated palace walls.

meals.breakfast: Pack a convenience store breakfast (7-Eleven or CU) before the hike – triangle kimbap, boiled eggs, banana milk (~5,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Mountain trail rest area or bring packed snacks. Alternatively, eat at a local restaurant near Gupabal Station – Doenjang Jjigae set (~10,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Seochon Village – Hyoja Dong Jalguksu (효자동 칼국수) for handmade knife-cut noodle soup, a warming winter meal (~9,000–12,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper hiking shoes and layer up for Bukhansan. Check trail conditions in advance as some paths may be icy in December. Hiking poles are recommended and can be rented near the trailhead.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (홍대) – Seoul's vibrant university district and the epicenter of K-indie culture, street art, and youth fashion. Explore Hongdae Free Market (if operating on weekends), browse vinyl record shops, and visit independent K-pop merchandise stores and webtoon-themed cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Sinchon and then to the nearby Yonsei University campus – a beautiful campus especially in winter. Continue to Ewha Womans University area for shopping and people-watching. Head to the nearby Gyeongui Line Forest Park (경의선 숲길) – a linear park built on an old railway line, popular with locals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the Saturday night atmosphere – live street performances (busking culture is huge here), neon-lit alleys, and club culture. Visit a Norebang (노래방 – Korean karaoke room) for an authentic K-culture experience (~15,000–25,000 KRW/hour for a private room).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or Insadong bakery (~7,000–10,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Hongdae – Yoogane Dak Galbi (유가네 닭갈비) for spicy stir-fried chicken and rice, a Hongdae institution (~12,000–15,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Hongdae – Gopchang Alley for grilled intestines (곱창구이) – adventurous but beloved by locals, with soju (~20,000–30,000 KRW including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Hongdae is lively and crowded. The area is safe but be aware of pickpockets in busy areas. Norebang is a quintessential K-culture activity – highly recommended for groups or solo travelers alike.

day_by_day.morning: Visit N Seoul Tower (남산타워) on Namsan Mountain. Take the Namsan Cable Car up (~9,500 KRW round trip) or hike the trail (~30 min). Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul's skyline. Browse the famous love lock fence and visit the observation deck. The tower opens at 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Myeongdong (명동) – Seoul's premier shopping and beauty district. Explore the pedestrian street lined with K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Laneige), street food carts, and international brands. Pick up skincare products and try street snacks. Visit Myeongdong Cathedral, a stunning Gothic-style landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Namdaemun Market (남대문시장), one of Korea's largest traditional markets, for evening shopping and street food. Browse Korean accessories, clothing, and kitchenware. Great place for budget souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area – try a traditional Korean breakfast at a nearby Hanjeongsik (한정식) restaurant with rice, soup, and multiple side dishes (~12,000–15,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch – Tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), Hotteok, Tornado Potato, and Egg Bread (~10,000–15,000 KRW for a variety of snacks)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong – Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자) for their famous Kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) and Mandu (dumplings), a Seoul institution since 1966 (~10,000–13,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely popular with tourists. Visit the street food stalls in the afternoon for the best selection. Many K-beauty shops offer free samples – take advantage! Myeongdong Kyoja often has queues but moves quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) – take the subway/bus to Suwon (~1 hour from central Seoul). Walk the 5.7km UNESCO World Heritage fortress walls surrounding the old city. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace inside the fortress grounds (~1,500 KRW). The fortress offers beautiful winter scenery and sweeping city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market area near the fortress – Paldalmun Market is great for local food. Return to Seoul in the late afternoon and relax at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) – an elevated highway converted into a beautiful urban stream. Walk along the lit stream path from Gwanghwamun toward Dongdaemun. In December, the stream may feature special winter light installations. End the walk at a cozy bar or café near Euljiro (을지로).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or convenience store (~5,000–8,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Suwon – Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) – the city is famous for its large, flavorful beef ribs. Try them at a local restaurant near the fortress (~25,000–35,000 KRW – a worthwhile splurge)
meals.dinner: Euljiro area – Pojangmacha (포장마차) street tent bar for Anju (drinking snacks) like Odeng (fish cake), Tteokbokki, and Sundubu Jjigae with Makgeolli (Korean rice wine) (~15,000–20,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is easily accessible via subway Line 1 to Suwon Station, then bus or taxi to the fortress. The fortress walk takes about 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Wear very warm layers as the fortress walls are fully exposed to winter winds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) in Yongsan – one of the largest museums in Asia with free admission. Explore Korean history from prehistoric times through the Joseon Dynasty. Don't miss the Silla gold crowns and the Goryeo celadon collection. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon (이태원) – Seoul's most international neighborhood, now reinvented as a trendy cultural hub. Explore the Gyeongnidan-gil area (경리단길) with its mix of independent restaurants, vintage shops, and specialty coffee roasters. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (리움미술관) for world-class Korean and international contemporary art (~20,000 KRW).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Haebangchon (HBC, 해방촌) – a hillside village above Itaewon with a creative, bohemian atmosphere. Browse art galleries, listen to live jazz, and enjoy the multicultural restaurant scene. Great area for a relaxed evening drink.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area – Egg Drop (에그드랍) café chain for avocado egg sandwiches, a trendy Korean breakfast option (~8,000–10,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: National Museum area – museum café or nearby Ichon-dong Korean restaurant for a Dosirak (Korean lunch box) set (~12,000–15,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Itaewon/Gyeongnidan-gil – Vatos Urban Tacos for Korean-Mexican fusion (a Seoul favorite) or a local Korean BBQ spot – Maple Tree House for premium but mid-range galbi (~25,000–35,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays, but today is Tuesday – perfect. The Leeum Museum has rotating exhibitions; check the current program online. Itaewon has transformed significantly in recent years into a sophisticated cultural district beyond its old reputation.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Gangnam (강남) – take the subway to the south side of the Han River. Visit COEX Mall (코엑스몰) – a massive underground mall featuring the famous Starfield Library (별마당 도서관), a stunning open library with thousands of books and a great café. Browse the aquarium and pop-up K-pop merchandise stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Bongeunsa Temple (봉은사) – a 1,200-year-old Buddhist temple dramatically situated next to the modern Gangnam skyline. Enjoy the contrast of ancient and ultra-modern Seoul. Then explore the Garosu-gil (가로수길) – a tree-lined street with boutique fashion shops, galleries, and upscale cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Han River (한강) at night – take a Han River Cruise (한강유람선) for 60 minutes of illuminated city views (~15,000–20,000 KRW). Alternatively, visit Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain (방포대교 달빛무지개분수) – the world's longest bridge fountain, beautifully lit at night (check seasonal schedule).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area (~7,000–10,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: COEX area – Food court inside COEX Mall for a variety of Korean dishes including Bibimbap, Sundubu, and Japchae (~10,000–15,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil – Hanilkwan (한일관) for a classic Hanjeongsik (Korean full-course meal) with multiple side dishes, a refined yet mid-range experience (~25,000–35,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Gangnam is best explored on foot between COEX, Bongeunsa, and Garosu-gil as they are within walking distance. The Han River cruise operates year-round but check winter schedules. December evenings by the river are very cold – bring hand warmers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) – the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in central Seoul near the hotel. Beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round and especially atmospheric during the holiday season. Explore the temple grounds and the Buddhist cultural center. Then walk to the nearby Unhyeongung Palace (운현궁) – the childhood home of King Gojong, less crowded than major palaces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Euljiro (을지로) district – Seoul's old printing and industrial quarter now transformed into one of the hippest neighborhoods in the city. Discover hidden speakeasy bars, vintage design shops, and creative spaces tucked between old printing workshops. Visit the Sewoon Sangga complex, a 1960s megastructure being reimagined as a creative hub.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul – Koreans celebrate Christmas as a romantic couple's holiday. Myeongdong and Gwanghwamun will be beautifully decorated with lights and Christmas markets. Attend a Christmas Eve concert or light show at Gwanghwamun Square. End the evening with a festive dinner.

meals.breakfast: Insadong area – Dawon Traditional Tea House (다원) for a traditional Korean tea ceremony breakfast with rice cakes and herbal teas (~12,000–15,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Euljiro – Euljiro 3-ga area hidden gem restaurants – try Yangpyeong Sundae (양평순대) for blood sausage soup, a local worker's staple (~8,000–10,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special – Book in advance at Gwanghwamun area restaurant. Try Balwoo Gongyang (발우공양) at Jogyesa Temple for exquisite Buddhist temple cuisine – a truly unique and memorable Christmas Eve dinner (~45,000–60,000 KRW – special occasion splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is a major event in Seoul. Expect crowds at major landmarks and shopping areas. Book dinner well in advance. Balwoo Gongyang is a Michelin-starred temple food restaurant – reservations are essential and worth every won for a unique cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning – visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) – the least visited of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces, offering a peaceful and uncrowded experience on a holiday. The palace garden is serene in winter. Then visit the Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관) next door (free admission) to understand the city's rapid transformation over the centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Mangwon Market (망원시장) in the Mapo district – a beloved local neighborhood market frequented by residents rather than tourists. Browse fresh produce, street food, and local goods. Walk along the Mangwon Hangang Park riverbank for a peaceful Han River winter walk.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Yeonnam-dong (연남동) neighborhood – nicknamed 'Yeonnamdong' and 'Seoul's Brooklyn.' Explore the Gyeongui Line Forest Park that runs through it, lined with independent restaurants, dessert cafés, and boutique shops. A perfect low-key Christmas evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area – treat yourself to a Christmas morning Korean bakery spread with cream bread, coffee, and pastries (~8,000–12,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market – street food feast: Twigim (fried snacks), Gimbap rolls, Bungeoppang (fish-shaped pastry with red bean), and Tteok (~8,000–12,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Yeonnam-dong – Palsaik Samgyeopsal (팔색삼겹살) for 8-flavor pork belly BBQ – a fun and festive Christmas dinner with various marinades cooked at the table (~18,000–25,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Seoul is a public holiday. Most major attractions remain open. Markets like Mangwon may have reduced hours – arrive before 15:00. Yeonnam-dong is a great alternative to the tourist-heavy areas and offers a glimpse of how young Seoulites actually live.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World Tower (롯데월드타워) in Songpa – take the subway to Jamsil Station. Ascend to the Seoul Sky Observatory on the 117th–123rd floors (~27,000 KRW) for breathtaking 360° views of Seoul and beyond on a clear winter day. The glass-floored skywalk is thrilling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the adjacent Seokchon Lake Park (석촌호수) – a beautiful lake park surrounding Lotte World. In winter, it may feature holiday light installations. Visit the nearby Olympic Park (올림픽공원) from the 1988 Seoul Olympics – a vast park with outdoor sculptures, a velodrome, and historic Mongchon Toseong earthen fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Final major K-culture experience – attend a K-pop concert, musical, or performance. Check current schedules at venues like the Olympic Gymnastics Arena, KSPO Dome, or smaller venues in Hongdae. Alternatively, visit a K-pop dance class for tourists in Hongdae (~30,000–50,000 KRW) or end with a final Norebang session.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area (~7,000–10,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Jamsil area – Lotte World Mall food court or nearby Jamsil Chicken Alley (잠실 치킨골목) for Korean fried chicken, a national obsession (~15,000–20,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Hongdae or Sinchon – Buk Chang Dong Soon Tofu (북창동순두부) for soft tofu stew (Sundubu Jjigae) with a stone pot of rice – comforting and warming (~10,000–14,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Book Seoul Sky Observatory tickets online in advance to save time. Check K-pop event schedules on platforms like Interpark or Melon Ticket well in advance. December is peak concert season in Seoul. The Olympic Park is free to enter and great for a peaceful afternoon walk.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – return to Gyeongbokgung Palace one last time for the 10:00 Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (if not seen on Day 2) or simply stroll through the palace grounds with fresh eyes after 13 days. Visit the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art – Government Complex Branch (MMCA Seoul) near the palace for a final dose of Korean contemporary art (free or ~4,000 KRW).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir hunting in Insadong and the Gyeongbokgung area. Pick up traditional Korean teas, Hanji paper products, celadon ceramics, Korean snacks (Choco Pie, Honey Butter Chips, traditional sweets), and K-beauty products. Pack bags and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Incheon Airport via AREX from Gwanghwamun/City Hall area. Allow at least 3 hours before your departure for check-in and security. Enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport before departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast – sit-down meal at a Jongno-gu local restaurant for Seolleongtang (설렁탕), a milky ox bone broth soup with rice – a Seoul classic (~10,000–13,000 KRW)
meals.lunch: Insadong – light lunch at a traditional Korean café with Bibimbap and Sikhye (~12,000–15,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport – enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport's restaurant level. Try Bibimbap or Korean BBQ at one of the airport restaurants (~15,000–25,000 KRW)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. The AREX direct train from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport takes approximately 43 minutes. You can also check in your luggage at Seoul Station's City Airport Terminal before boarding the train. Keep T-money card topped up for the final journey.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — skip morning activities. Private luxury transfer arranged via chauffeured black car service to Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Check-in, unpack, and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Bukchon Hanok Village (10-minute walk from hotel). Stroll the lantern-lit alleyways of this preserved traditional neighborhood, admire the tile-roofed hanok houses, and soak in the atmospheric December ambiance. Visit the Bukchon Traditional Culture Center for a brief introduction to Korean heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Jungsik Seoul (2 Michelin stars, Gangnam) — book private transfer. Experience Chef Jung Sik Yim's modern Korean cuisine with seasonal tasting menus. Return to hotel for rest after long-haul travel.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport lounge meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack at hotel upon check-in — traditional Korean tea and rice cakes arranged by concierge
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul — modern Korean fine dining tasting menu (approx. ₩250,000–₩350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Request airport meet-and-greet service and fast-track immigration if available. Confirm hotel concierge for all upcoming restaurant reservations upon check-in. Dress warmly — Seoul in December averages -2°C to 5°C.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace (literally steps from the hotel). Witness the elaborate Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the Gwanghwamun Gate (10:00 & 14:00). Explore the grand throne hall Geunjeongjeon and the serene Hyangwonjeong Pavilion dusted with winter frost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds for deep cultural context. Afterward, explore Insadong's premium art galleries and antique shops — pick up certified Korean celadon ceramics or hanji paper art as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mingles (1 Michelin star, Gangnam) — Chef Mingoo Kang's Korean-European fusion. Book private chauffeur for the evening. Post-dinner, enjoy a premium makgeolli tasting at a curated bar in Insadong.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request traditional Korean breakfast (doenjang jjigae, rice, banchan) or Western option
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang near Gyeongbokgung — legendary ginseng chicken soup restaurant, a Seoul institution
meals.dinner: Mingles — Korean-inspired fine dining tasting menu (approx. ₩230,000–₩300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is a 2-minute walk from the hotel. Wear hanbok for free palace entry — rental shops are nearby. The palace is stunning in winter with occasional snow.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day K-culture immersion experience: Hanbok dressing session with a master craftsperson at a premium hanbok atelier in Jongno-gu. Followed by a private calligraphy (seoye) and hanji art workshop led by a certified cultural artisan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) on a guided tour. The winter landscape of bare trees and frozen ponds offers a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere unique to December. Explore Nakseonjae complex within the palace grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at La Yeon (3 Michelin stars, The Shilla Hotel) — the pinnacle of Korean haute cuisine. Floor-to-ceiling views of Seoul paired with an exquisite seasonal Korean tasting menu. Dress code: smart formal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang at Templestay Information Center — award-winning Korean Buddhist temple cuisine (hansik), a meditative and refined dining experience
meals.dinner: La Yeon, The Shilla Seoul — Korean fine dining (approx. ₩350,000–₩450,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour in advance — limited capacity. La Yeon requires reservations months ahead; confirm with concierge immediately.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul — for a peaceful morning meditation experience. Participate in a private temple stay morning program (optional): 108 prostrations, meditation, and monk's tea ceremony.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Cheonggyecheon Stream promenade and then head to Gwangjang Market for an authentic deep-dive into Korean street food culture. Browse the market's premium section for hand-woven silk fabric and vintage Korean goods.
day_by_day.evening: Gangnam evening: Visit the COEX Starfield Library for architectural wonder, then dinner at Gaon (3 Michelin stars) — a transcendent Korean royal court cuisine experience with an extraordinary wine and traditional liquor pairing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market premium tasting experience — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, yukhoe (beef tartare) — curated with a local food guide
meals.dinner: Gaon, Gangnam — Korean royal court cuisine tasting menu (approx. ₩400,000–₩500,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is best experienced with a knowledgeable food guide — arrange through hotel concierge. Private transfer to Gangnam recommended (approx. 30 min from hotel).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage site of Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon (approx. 1 hour by private car). Explore the magnificent 18th-century fortress walls, Hwahongmun Gate, and the surrounding traditional village. Private cultural guide included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Suwon: Visit Haenggung Palace (Hwaseong Haenggung) and enjoy a private traditional Korean performance (taekkyeon martial arts or court music). Return to Seoul by private car.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Kwon Sooksoo in Gangnam — intimate, reservation-only Korean fine dining by celebrated chef Kwon Woo-joong. Afterward, evening drinks at a premium rooftop bar in Gangnam with panoramic Seoul skyline views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early start recommended)
meals.lunch: Traditional Suwon galbi (short rib) lunch at Yeonpo Galbi — Suwon is famous for its galbi, a must-try regional specialty
meals.dinner: Kwon Sooksoo — intimate Korean tasting menu (approx. ₩280,000–₩380,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday may mean crowds at Hwaseong — early departure (9:00) recommended. Dress in layers; fortress walls are exposed to winter wind.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a quieter, more residential counterpart to Bukchon. Visit independent art galleries, the studio of the late poet Yun Dong-ju, and artisan coffee roasters. Attend a private Korean tea ceremony (darye) at a traditional tearoom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums. Explore the permanent collection of Korean art and artifacts spanning 5,000 years of history. Hire a private museum guide for a curated 2-hour tour.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ryunique (2 Michelin stars, Gangnam) — Chef Ryu Tae-hwan's innovative contemporary Korean cuisine. Post-dinner, visit a premium norebang (karaoke) private room experience at Su Norebang — luxury private suites with premium sound systems.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Cafe Onion Anguk or Anthracite Coffee — premium brunch in a beautifully converted space near Seochon Village
meals.dinner: Ryunique — contemporary Korean fine dining (approx. ₩250,000–₩330,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays — Sunday visit is perfectly timed. Norebang is a quintessential K-culture experience; luxury venues offer premium liquor and food service.

day_by_day.morning: Private K-pop and Korean Wave (Hallyu) cultural experience: Visit the SM Town COEX Artium for an immersive K-pop exhibition. Then, a private behind-the-scenes tour of a K-pop entertainment district in Gangnam with a cultural expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong — Seoul's luxury fashion district. Visit flagship stores of Korean luxury brands (MCM, Gentle Monster, Tamburins). Optionally, book a premium Korean skincare consultation at Amorepacific flagship store.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito Seoul (exclusive Japanese-Korean omakase) or Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul at Lotte Hotel — a world-class French fine dining experience with Korean seasonal ingredients. Evening stroll along the Hangang River with a private sunset/twilight cruise.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a premium Cheongdam-dong café — try a high-end Korean fusion café experience
meals.dinner: Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul or premium omakase — (approx. ₩300,000–₩500,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hangang River cruise in December offers stunning winter city views. Bring warm outerwear. K-pop cultural tours should be pre-arranged through a specialist local guide.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a Korean culinary master — learn to prepare royal court hansik dishes: kimchi jeon, galbi jjim (braised short ribs), and japchae. Class held in a traditional hanok kitchen near Jongno-gu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ihwa Mural Village on Naksan Mountain for street art and panoramic views of Seoul. Explore the quirky, creative neighborhood beloved by artists. Descend to Hyehwa (Daehangno) — Seoul's theater district — for a browse through independent bookshops and art spaces.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live performance at the National Theater of Korea — check schedule for traditional gugak (Korean classical music) or contemporary Korean dance performance. Pre-theater dinner at a premium restaurant near Namsan.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared in the morning cooking class as part of the experience
meals.dinner: Namsangol Hanok Village area premium Korean restaurant — try a refined version of gujeolpan (royal nine-section dish) and traditional Korean royal cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book National Theater of Korea tickets in advance. The cooking class is a highly personal and memorable cultural experience — arrange through a premium culinary tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Nami Island and Petite France (approx. 1.5 hours by private car). Nami Island in winter is a magical, quiet landscape — bare ginkgo and metasequoia trees draped in frost. The island gained global fame from the K-drama 'Winter Sonata.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Petite France — a whimsical French-themed cultural village in the mountains near Chuncheon. Explore the colorful architecture, Le Petit Prince exhibitions, and puppet shows. Optional: stop at Garden of Morning Calm for the winter illumination festival.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Dinner at Hanilkwan in Gangnam — a historic, premium Korean restaurant beloved for its traditional royal-style cuisine. One of Seoul's most storied dining institutions.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early start — depart by 8:00)
meals.lunch: Dak galbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) lunch in Chuncheon — the dish originated here and is a regional specialty
meals.dinner: Hanilkwan, Gangnam — traditional Korean royal cuisine (approx. ₩150,000–₩250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nami Island requires a ferry crossing — dress very warmly. Garden of Morning Calm Winter Illumination runs November through January — a spectacular evening light festival worth timing your visit around.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (lesser-visited, intimate atmosphere) and the Seoul Museum of History nearby. Private guided tour focusing on the Joseon Dynasty's cultural and political history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the premium Lotte World Tower and Sky31 Observatory for breathtaking panoramic views of Seoul. Visit the Lotte Museum of Art for contemporary Korean and international exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve dinner at Dine & Wine at Park Hyatt Seoul — premium Western-Korean fusion with exceptional wine cellar. Seoul celebrates Christmas Eve vibrantly — enjoy the festive atmosphere in Myeongdong with its dazzling Christmas lights and street performances. Visit Myeongdong Cathedral illuminated for the season.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — legendary hand-made kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings), a Seoul institution
meals.dinner: Park Hyatt Seoul special Christmas Eve dinner — (approx. ₩300,000–₩400,000 per person with wine pairing)

day_by_day.notes: Seoul is festive and lively on Christmas Eve. Book Christmas Eve dinner well in advance. Myeongdong is extremely crowded but magical during the holiday season.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Christmas morning: Enjoy a luxurious extended breakfast at the hotel. Optional: Private sunrise visit to Bugaksan Mountain trail (behind Gyeongbokgung) for a peaceful winter hike with views over the city — a serene Christmas morning experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Asia's finest private art museums, housing Korean national treasures alongside contemporary global art. Explore the stunning architecture by Mario Botta, Jean Nouvel, and Rem Koolhaas.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day special dinner at Alain Ducasse at Chosun Palace (Lotte Hotel) or The Library at Four Seasons Hotel Seoul — a world-class festive dining experience. Toast the holiday with premium Korean champagne alternatives (sparkling makgeolli or imported champagne).

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel Christmas breakfast — request special holiday spread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Leeum Museum café or a nearby premium Itaewon restaurant
meals.dinner: Alain Ducasse at Chosun Palace or Four Seasons Seoul — Christmas special menu (approx. ₩400,000–₩600,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions may have reduced hours on Christmas Day — confirm in advance. Christmas in Seoul is a public holiday with a festive atmosphere. The Leeum Museum is a must for art and culture lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive Korean spa (jjimjilbang) experience at Dragon Hill Spa — a premium multi-floor Korean bathhouse. Enjoy various themed sauna rooms, hot and cold plunge pools, and traditional Italy towel body scrub (seshin) performed by a professional.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hongdae — Seoul's vibrant youth culture and indie arts district. Visit premium vintage shops, independent record stores, and contemporary art galleries. Experience the street performance culture unique to this area.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at Charles H. Bar in the Four Seasons Hotel Seoul — one of Asia's best bars. Dinner at Onjium (1 Michelin star) — a deeply researched and beautifully presented Korean traditional cuisine experience rooted in historical recipes.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Hongdae area premium brunch — try a Korean-Western fusion café or a well-regarded ramen specialist in the area
meals.dinner: Onjium — traditional Korean historical cuisine (approx. ₩250,000–₩350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dragon Hill Spa is open 24 hours — morning is the best time to avoid weekend crowds. The seshin body scrub is a transformative cultural experience. Book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning stroll through Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds one last time at dawn — a private, peaceful farewell to Seoul's most iconic landmark. Visit the National Palace Museum of Korea within the grounds for any last cultural artifacts you wish to see.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute premium shopping at Shinsegae Department Store (Myeongdong) — Korea's oldest and most prestigious department store. Pick up premium Korean beauty products (Sulwhasoo, History of Whoo), food gifts (premium Korean teas, artisan gochujang, premium seaweed), and luxury Korean fashion items.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations: Final dinner at Seorae Village (Seoul's French Quarter) or a farewell meal at a beloved restaurant of your choice from the trip. Private luxury chauffeur transfer to Incheon International Airport — allow 2 hours minimum for international departure.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — leisurely final morning meal
meals.lunch: Premium Korean BBQ farewell lunch at Maple Tree House (Itaewon) — one of Seoul's finest hanwoo (Korean wagyu) beef experiences
meals.dinner: Light pre-departure dinner at the airport — Incheon has excellent premium dining options in the departure terminal

day_by_day.notes: Check out of hotel and store luggage with concierge during morning activities. Confirm departure transfer with hotel the evening before. Incheon Airport is approximately 60–75 minutes by private car from central Seoul. Allow ample time for luxury duty-free shopping at Incheon, which is world-class.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX
